(a) ANALYTICAL PHYSICS READOUT - ISS / LEO Station vs Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom). MODEL-DERIVED from the physics_ranker equations (E1-E7) and the project habitat constants; none of these numbers is a PSI measurement.
  Oxygen: 21% O2 vs 21% = a 0% to 0% relative increase (increase). At 101.3 kPa total pressure the O2 partial pressure is 21.3 kPa vs 21.3 kPa, so the extra hazard comes from the larger O2 mole fraction (less N2 diluent), not from a higher pO2. Flame-spread scaling (E7, V ~ P^0.75 X_O2^2): x1 to x1 vs x1 for Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom) (relative to 1 atm / 21% O2).
  Convection: at 0 g natural-convection velocity is u_b = 0 cm/s (E1: u_b = C_b sqrt(g g0 Lc), C_b = 0.5, Lc = 5 cm) vs 35 cm/s at 1 g. The ~0 cm/s figure is the habitat reference / effective velocity from the project constants (u_eff reference 8 to 20 cm/s), NOT a PSI measurement. Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom) ventilation: 35 to 60 cm/s (NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 — natural upward buoyant convection 35–60 cm/s).
  Ventilation hazard (E3): with mid-range forced flow (13.9 cm/s) the mixed-convection velocity is u_eff = 13.9 cm/s, hazard factor H = 0.99; Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom) (47.5 cm/s, 1 g): u_eff = 59 cm/s, H = 0.41. Both sit on the peak-hazard band (~12 cm/s) where a low-velocity flow supplies O2 without blowing the flame off.
  Limiting O2 concentration (E4, calibration: LOC at 1 g / 1 atm / quiescent = 17% assumed; slow-flow minimum = 0.88 x that): modelled LOC at this flow is 15% for ISS / LEO Station and 19.6% for Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom), versus 32.4% for quiescent 0 g air (no flow, flame quenches) - low-velocity convection is what pulls LOC down toward its minimum (the ventilation paradox). The habitat atmosphere then exceeds the modelled LOC by 6 O2 points (21% vs 15%) against 1.4 points on Earth Analogs (Submarine / Mine / Cleanroom): elevated O2 does not move the LOC itself, it widens the margin above it, which is what accelerates flame spread (E7).
  Qualitative physics background (NASA-STD-6001 / partial-gravity combustion literature; NOT measured in the PSI files here): reduced buoyancy at 0.16 g gives weaker, longer-lived, more sooty and radiation-dominated flames, while an O2-enriched, N2-lean atmosphere raises flame temperature and burning rate; the two effects compound. The 1 g reference (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) is not part of the PSI tables.

provenance_note: Every row is parsed from files downloaded from psi.nasa.gov (see source_files). Units are converted only where the file itself states the unit (see /api/conversions); quantities a file does not state are NULL. gravity_g (actual gravity) = 0.0 is a project-level ISS / Cygnus flight baseline (gravity_inferred=true; gravity_source says whether the PSI JSON names ISS/Cygnus/MSG/CIR or the value is user-stated) and never tabulated; row-level ground tags would set 1.0. effective_gravity_g is a HEURISTIC PROXY (flow-equivalent), never measured partial gravity (see /api/effective-gravity). Empirical predictors are exposed only if they beat dummy baselines under group cross-validation (/api/model-audit); otherwise the nearest real experimental tests are returned. Research triage, not a certified determination.
